primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: EAST (SeSAME) syndrome due to KCNJ10 loss of function
mechanism: KCNJ10 encodes the inward-rectifier potassium channel Kir4.1. In the distal convoluted tubule, basolateral Kir4.1-dependent potassium conductance is required for normal epithelial electrical and potassium-sensing physiology that supports sodium-chloride reabsorption. Loss of Kir4.1 produces a salt-wasting tubulopathy with hypokalemia and accompanies the neurologic and auditory phenotype of EAST/SeSAME syndrome.
vignette: A 9-year-old boy has epilepsy, gait ataxia, and bilateral sensorineural hearing loss. Laboratory studies show persistent hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis despite normal blood pressure. Genetic testing identifies a biallelic loss-of-function variant in KCNJ10.
lead: Which of the following renal cellular abnormalities most directly results from this mutation?
correct: Reduced basolateral potassium conductance in distal convoluted tubule cells
distractors: Loss of the apical sodium-potassium-2 chloride cotransporter in the thick ascending limb
Loss of apical potassium secretion through ROMK in the thick ascending limb
Constitutive activation of the epithelial sodium channel in collecting-duct principal cells
Loss of the apical sodium-chloride cotransporter itself in distal convoluted tubule cells
distractor_notes: NKCC2 loss causes a classic Bartter phenotype but is not the defect encoded by KCNJ10.
ROMK loss is another Bartter mechanism and does not explain the KCNJ10-associated neurologic and auditory syndrome.
ENaC gain of function causes Liddle syndrome with hypertension rather than salt wasting and hypotension/normal pressure.
KCNJ10 encodes the basolateral Kir4.1 potassium channel, not NCC; NCC activity is secondarily affected by altered distal-tubule physiology.
key_expl: KCNJ10 encodes Kir4.1, a basolateral inward-rectifier potassium channel expressed in the distal convoluted tubule and in neural/inner-ear tissues. Loss of Kir4.1 disrupts distal-tubule potassium conductance and salt handling, producing the renal component of EAST/SeSAME syndrome together with epilepsy, ataxia, and sensorineural deafness.
objective: Link KCNJ10 loss in EAST/SeSAME syndrome to impaired basolateral Kir4.1 potassium conductance in the distal convoluted tubule.
